citations.sentence: And, Charles, upon condition thou wilt swear To pay him tribute and submit thyself, Thou shalt be placed as viceroy under him, And still enjoy the regal dignity.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: The proudest peer in the realm shall not wear a head on his shoulders unless he pay me tribute; there shall not a maid be married but she shall pay to me her maidenhead ere they have it.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: Needs must you lay your heart at his dispose, Subjected tribute to commanding love, Against whose fury and unmatched force The aweless lion could not wage the fight, Nor keep his princely heart from Richard’s hand.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: Now he goes, With no less presence, but with much more love Than young Alcides when he did redeem The virgin tribute paid by howling Troy To the sea-monster: I stand for sacrifice; The rest aloof are the Dardanian wives, With bleared visages come forth to view The issue of th’ exploit.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: Take some remembrance of us as a tribute, Not as fee.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: Off goes his bonnet to an oyster-wench; A brace of draymen bid God speed him well, And had the tribute of his supple knee, With “Thanks, my countrymen, my loving friends”, As were our England in reversion his, And he our subjects’ next degree in hope.

citations.author: William Shakespeare
citations.work: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
citations.sentence: Me, poor man, my library Was dukedom large enough: of temporal royalties He thinks me now incapable; confederates, So dry he was for sway, wi’ th’ King of Naples To give him annual tribute, do him homage, Subject his coronet to his crown, and bend The dukedom, yet unbow’d—alas, poor Milan!— To most ignoble stooping.
